cities.name: Glasgow
cities.summary: Scotland's biggest city mixes Victorian grandeur, major museums and a lively music scene with easy escapes to Loch Lomond.

cities.name: Birmingham
cities.summary: Birmingham pairs canals, industrial heritage and top museums with one of Britain's strongest food scenes.

cities.name: Bath
cities.summary: Elegant Georgian streets, Roman remains and spa culture make Bath one of England's most atmospheric small cities.

cities.name: Oxford
cities.summary: Oxford's dreaming spires, college quads and riverside walks create one of England's classic heritage city breaks.

clusters.name: Historic Colleges
attractions: University Church of St Mary the Virgin

cities.name: Cambridge
cities.summary: Cambridge combines world-famous colleges, river punting and fine museums in a compact, handsome city.

cities.name: York
cities.summary: York packs Roman, Viking and medieval history into a walkable walled centre full of lanes, towers and tea rooms.

cities.name: Bristol
cities.summary: Creative Bristol blends maritime history, street art, harbourside culture and easy access to southwest food and cider.

cities.name: Belfast
cities.summary: Belfast pairs Titanic history, political murals and lively pubs with a fast-rising restaurant and music scene.

cities.name: Cardiff
cities.summary: Cardiff offers a compact capital mix of castle history, rejuvenated waterfront and stadium energy.

cities.name: Scottish Highlands
cities.summary: The Scottish Highlands deliver dramatic glens, lochs and mountain scenery, with Fort William and Glen Coe as classic bases.

cities.name: Galway
cities.summary: Galway is Ireland's west-coast cultural capital, loved for trad music, seafood and quick access to Connemara and the Aran ferries.

cities.name: Cork
cities.summary: Cork mixes a confident food scene, riverside streets and easy access to castles and coves in southwest Ireland.

cities.name: Killarney
cities.summary: Killarney is a classic base for lakes, mountain views and manor houses at the gateway to the Ring of Kerry.

cities.name: Limerick
cities.summary: Limerick layers Norman history, riverside walks and a growing arts scene along the River Shannon.

cities.name: Kilkenny
cities.summary: Kilkenny's compact medieval streets, castle and craft culture make it one of Ireland's easiest and richest short breaks.

cities.name: Cliffs of Moher
cities.summary: Ireland's most dramatic sea cliffs rise above the Atlantic, with broad coastal views, birdlife and wave-cut rock scenery.

cities.name: Ring of Kerry
cities.summary: This famous Kerry loop combines Atlantic viewpoints, beaches, stone forts and mountain passes best explored by car or tour.

cities.name: Florence
cities.summary: Florence is a Renaissance showpiece of art, domes and palaces, with superb food and walkable streets along the Arno.

clusters.name: Duomo & Piazza Core
attractions: Cathedral of Santa Maria del Fiore

cities.name: Milan
cities.summary: Milan blends blockbuster art, cathedral grandeur, fashion districts and aperitivo energy with fast rail links across Italy.

cities.name: Naples
cities.summary: Naples delivers intense street life, top archaeology, pizza culture and easy access to Pompeii, Vesuvius and the bay.

cities.name: Pisa
cities.summary: Pisa offers far more than its famous leaning tower, with a handsome riverfront and one of Tuscany's great cathedral squares.

cities.name: Siena
cities.summary: Siena's shell-shaped piazza, Gothic cathedral and contrada traditions make it Tuscany's most atmospheric hill city.

cities.name: Bologna
cities.summary: Bologna charms with arcaded streets, medieval towers and one of Italy's best food cultures.

clusters.name: San Luca & Aperitivo
attractions: Sanctuary of the Madonna di San Luca

cities.name: Verona
cities.summary: Verona combines Roman ruins, river views and romantic lanes beyond its famous Shakespeare associations.

cities.name: Lake Como
cities.summary: Lake Como pairs elegant villas, mountain-backed ferry rides and pretty lakeside towns around deep blue water.

cities.name: Cinque Terre
cities.summary: Cinque Terre strings together five colourful Ligurian villages with coastal paths, vineyards and sea views.

cities.name: Amalfi
cities.summary: Amalfi offers a historic maritime centre, dramatic sea cliffs and easy boat links along the Amalfi Coast.

cities.name: Positano
cities.summary: Positano is the Amalfi Coast's glamorous cliffside village, known for beaches, boutiques and postcard sea views.

cities.name: Sorrento
cities.summary: Sorrento combines lemon-scented lanes, clifftop views and excellent transport links to Capri, Pompeii and the Amalfi Coast.

cities.name: Capri
cities.summary: Capri is a chic island escape of sea caves, dramatic viewpoints and stylish piazzas above brilliantly blue water.

cities.name: Palermo
cities.summary: Palermo layers Arab-Norman monuments, vibrant markets and grand Sicilian streets with the sea close by.

cities.name: Catania
cities.summary: Catania mixes dark lava-stone baroque, buzzing markets and nightlife at the foot of Mount Etna.

cities.name: Taormina
cities.summary: Taormina sits high above the Ionian Sea, famous for its Greek theatre, views of Etna and elegant resort atmosphere.

cities.name: Bari
cities.summary: Bari combines a lively old port, white-stone lanes and strong Puglian food culture on the Adriatic coast.

cities.name: Matera
cities.summary: Matera's ancient cave districts create one of Italy's most distinctive cityscapes, especially at golden hour and by night.

clusters.name: Rock Churches
attractions: Chiesa Rupestre di Santa Lucia alle Malve

cities.name: Vatican City
cities.summary: Vatican City concentrates some of the world's greatest religious art and architecture within a tiny walled state.

cities.name: San Marino
cities.summary: San Marino packs mountaintop fortresses, panoramic lanes and tax-free shopping into one of Europe's smallest states.

cities.name: Monaco
cities.summary: Monaco combines yacht-filled glamour, palace views and Formula 1 streets in a tiny but spectacular Riviera state.
